findings.title: in.Verify.Skipped branch of notProven never exercised
findings.detail: The task spec requires the Not proven section to seed from `in.Verify when Overridden != "" or Skipped` (skeleton.go:395-401). No fixture in internal/finish/skeleton_test.go ever sets VerifyRecord.Skipped = true; only Overridden is covered (fullRun's Verify at diff-relative test line ~649). The literal 'verification — skipped, the run had no commands to run' string and its whole code path are untested — a regression or typo there would not be caught.

findings.title: Legacy slice-less wave_committed events never tested for the documented floor-to-1 behaviour
findings.detail: BuildShipped's doc comment and the task brief both call out that a commit's slice is 'floored to 1 exactly as timingKeyOf does', covering an event written before slices existed (missing 'slice' key, decodes to 0). The test helper `committed(w, sl, a int, ...)` in internal/finish/skeleton_test.go:30 always supplies an explicit slice, and no fixture omits the key or passes 0/absent slice data. This backward-compatibility path — explicitly named as required behaviour — has zero coverage.

findings.title: 'task omitted when 0' formatting never asserted for a fully-rendered follow-up line
findings.detail: followUpWhere's `if f.Task != 0 { where += "/task %d" }` (task-omission rule from the brief) is only exercised by a Severity:"nit" fixture (skeleton_test.go, fullRun FollowUps, Wave: new(1) with no Task) — but nit/minor items never go through followUpLine/followUpWhere at all, only through the count line (bucketFollowUps only sends blocking/major to `full`). No blocking or major fixture has Wave set with Task==0, so the actual rendered text for a wave-only (no task) blocking/major follow-up is never checked against a golden.

findings.title: Markdown table cell escaping (cellEscaper) is untested
findings.detail: cell()/cellEscaper exists specifically to protect the What-shipped table from a task title or SHA containing '|' or a newline, but no test fixture ever includes such a character in a title or SHA. If the escaping regresses (e.g. only single-char replace, or breaks the table structure), TestRenderSkeletonGolden and friends would not detect it since none of the fixtures need escaping.

findings.title: otherSeverities / unknown-severity counting path untested
findings.detail: countsLine/otherSeverities is written to count any follow-up severity beyond the known blocking/major/minor/nit set ('Anything else a reviewer wrote is counted too, under its own name'), but no test fixture uses an unrecognised Severity value, so this defensive branch and its sort-for-determinism guarantee are never exercised.

findings.title: Numbers block's nil-to-empty-slice WaveTimings substitution untested
findings.detail: `timings := in.WaveTimings; if timings == nil { timings = []WaveTiming{} }` only matters when in.Internal != nil and len(in.WaveTimings) == 0 (so the early 'none' return is skipped) — a case that would otherwise marshal `"wave_timings": null`. No golden fixture combines a non-nil Internal with a genuinely absent WaveTimings, so this substitution (json:[] vs null) is never checked.

findings.title: BuildDecisions' nil *bundle.State guard untested
findings.detail: `if st != nil && st.Disposition != nil` guards against a nil State pointer, but every test call passes a non-nil *bundle.State (either with or without a Disposition); none passes st == nil. A regression that panics or misbehaves on a nil State (a legitimate input per the signature) would not be caught.
